title: Addition and Subtraction of 6-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Addition and Subtraction Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Add and subtract whole numbers of at least 6 digits; use a range of techniques to perform and check written and mental calculations, including estimation, adding and subtracting in columns, building up and breaking down numbers, rounding off and compensating, and using addition and subtraction as inverse operations.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 addition and subtraction worksheets: 6-digit column addition and subtraction, mental strategies, estimating and word problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Line up the units; carry and borrow carefully.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write the numbers in columns with the units lined up.
  • Carry 1 to the next column when a column adds to 10 or more.
  • Borrow from the next column when the top digit is too small. Across a 0, borrow from the next place that is not 0.
  • Estimate first, and check subtraction with addition.

Examples

Example

500 000 − 236 457

borrow across the zeros

check: 263 543 + 236 457 = 500 000

Answer: 263 543

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to carryWrite the carried 1 above the next column.
Borrowing across 0Go to the next place that is not 0.
Wrong columnsLine up the units.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about addition and subtraction?
faq.a: Add and subtract whole numbers of at least 6 digits, using estimation, rounding off, compensating and inverse operations to check.

faq.q: How do I check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number you took away.
To see if the answer is sensible.

items.e: 6,507 is between 6 and 7. Look only at the tenths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 7.

items.q: Round 23,09 to a whole number.
items.e: 23,09 is between 23 and 24. Look only at the tenths digit: 0. It is 4 or less, so round down to 23.

items.q: Round 48,45 kg to the nearest kilogram.
items.e: 48,45 kg is between 48 kg and 49 kg. Look only at the tenths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 48 kg. Do not round twice (48,45 → 48,5 → 49).

items.q: Round 2,7 ℓ to the nearest litre.
items.e: 2,7 ℓ is between 2 ℓ and 3 ℓ. Look only at the tenths digit: 7. It is 5 or more, so round up to 3 ℓ.

items.q: Which calculation checks 624 150 − 387 462 = 236 688?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 236 688 + 387 462 = 624 150. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 800 403 − 256 718 = 543 685?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 543 685 + 256 718 = 800 403. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 357 286 + 264 519 = 621 805?
items.e: Subtraction is the inverse of addition. Take one number away from the answer: 621 805 − 264 519 = 357 286. You get the other number, so the answer is right.

items.q: 738 205 − 249 687 = 488 518. Which number sentence is also true?
items.e: The three numbers make a fact family. The two smaller numbers add to make the biggest: 488 518 + 249 687 = 738 205.

items.q: 95 412 − 47 658 = 47 754. Which number sentence is also true?
items.e: The three numbers make a fact family. The two smaller numbers add to make the biggest: 47 754 + 47 658 = 95 412.

A theme park had 452 600 visitors in the summer. In the winter it had 186 750 fewer visitors. How many visitors did it have in the summer and winter altogether?
items.e: Step 1, visitors in the winter: 452 600 − 186 750 = 265 850. Step 2, both together: 452 600 + 265 850 = 718 450.

items.q: A website had 286 450 visitors in January and 315 780 visitors in February. Another website had 650 000 visitors in the same two months. How many more visitors did the other website have?
items.e: Step 1, visitors to the first website: 286 450 + 315 780 = 602 230. Step 2, find the difference: 650 000 − 602 230 = 47 770.

items.q: Jabu’s family drove 12 486 km in 2 023 and 14 075 km in 2 024. In 2 025 they drove 11 938 km. How much further did they drive in 2 023 and 2 024 together than in 2 025?
items.e: Step 1, 2 023 and 2 024: 12 486 km + 14 075 km = 26 561 km. Step 2, find the difference: 26 561 km − 11 938 km = 14 623 km.

items.q: A theatre sold 65 820 tickets in 2 024. In 2 025 it sold 8 475 fewer tickets. How many tickets did it sell in the two years?
Andile’s dad is a lorry driver. This year he plans to drive 100 000 km. He drove 45 120 km from January to June and 37 465 km from July to October. How many kilometres are left to drive this year?
items.e: Step 1, kilometres driven: 45 120 km + 37 465 km = 82 585 km. Step 2, kilometres left: 100 000 km − 82 585 km = 17 415 km. Check: 17 415 km + 82 585 km = 100 000 km.

items.q: Ashford has 74 385 people. Brookfield has 18 640 more people than Ashford. How many people live in the two towns altogether?
items.e: Step 1, people in Brookfield: 74 385 + 18 640 = 93 025. Step 2, both together: 74 385 + 93 025 = 167 410.

items.q: A delivery company’s vans must drive 250 000 km this year. They drove 98 476 km in the first four months and 87 950 km in the next four months. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Step 1, kilometres driven: 98 476 km + 87 950 km = 186 426 km. Step 2, kilometres left: 250 000 km − 186 426 km = 63 574 km. Check: 63 574 km + 186 426 km = 250 000 km.

items.q: On Saturday, 34 568 fans watched a match at one stadium and 28 795 fans watched a match at another. On Sunday, 72 000 fans watched the cup final. How many more fans watched the cup final than the two Saturday matches?
items.e: Step 1, fans on Saturday: 34 568 + 28 795 = 63 363. Step 2, find the difference: 72 000 − 63 363 = 8 637.

items.q: A city library had 64 005 books. It gave away 8 368 old books and then bought 5 275 new books. How many books does it have now?
items.e: Step 1, after giving away: 64 005 − 8 368 = 55 637. Step 2, after buying: 55 637 + 5 275 = 60 912.

items.q: In 2 024, 128 460 people visited a museum. In 2 025, 15 875 fewer people visited. How many people visited in the two years?
A warehouse had 125 400 parcels. It sent out 87 965 parcels, then a lorry delivered 46 580 more. How many parcels are in the warehouse now?
items.e: Step 1, after sending: 125 400 − 87 965 = 37 435. Step 2, after the delivery: 37 435 + 46 580 = 84 015.

items.q: A stadium has 90 000 tickets for a concert. It sold 46 758 tickets on the first day and 28 965 tickets on the second day. How many tickets are left?
Anika’s family drove 12 486 km in 2 023 and 14 075 km in 2 024. In 2 025 they drove 11 938 km. How much further did they drive in 2 023 and 2 024 together than in 2 025?
items.e: Step 1, 2 023 and 2 024: 12 486 km + 14 075 km = 26 561 km. Step 2, find the difference: 26 561 km − 11 938 km = 14 623 km.

items.q: When the Dhillon family bought their van, the odometer showed 48 579 km. Now it shows 213 006 km. How far have they driven the van?
items.e: Find the distance between the two readings, so subtract. 213 006 − 48 579 = 164 427. Check: 164 427 + 48 579 = 213 006.

items.q: One BC ferry sailed 48 675 km in the spring and 52 390 km in the summer. How far did it sail in the two seasons?
items.e: Put the two seasons together, so add. 48 675 + 52 390 = 101 065. Check: 101 065 − 52 390 = 48 675.

items.q: Volunteers counted 486 275 sockeye salmon on the Adams River in one week and 357 948 the next week. How many sockeye did they count in the two weeks?
items.e: Put the two weeks together, so add. 486 275 + 357 948 = 844 223. Check: 844 223 − 357 948 = 486 275.

items.q: Learners in a school district set a goal to walk and bike 300 000 km to school this year. So far they have logged 186 475 km. How many more kilometres do they need?
items.e: Find what is still needed, so subtract. 300 000 − 186 475 = 113 525. Check: 113 525 + 186 475 = 300 000.

items.q: A SkyTrain station had 248 675 riders in September. In October it had 36 480 more riders than in September. How many riders did it have in the two months?
items.e: Step 1, October’s riders: 248 675 + 36 480 = 285 155. Step 2, both together: 248 675 + 285 155 = 533 830.

items.q: A tree nursery had 450 000 cedar seedlings. It sent 286 475 to be planted in forests. Then it grew 175 650 more. How many seedlings does the nursery have now?
items.e: Step 1, after sending some out: 450 000 − 286 475 = 163 525. Step 2, after growing more: 163 525 + 175 650 = 339 175.

items.q: A library system in the Lower Mainland has 750 000 books. 286 450 books are checked out and 48 675 are being repaired. How many books are on the shelves?
items.e: Step 1, books not on the shelves: 286 450 + 48 675 = 335 125. Step 2, books on the shelves: 750 000 − 335 125 = 414 875.
